newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends narrowly mixed, still in range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends narrowly mixed, still in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended narrowly mixed Thursday in an active session, with prices still bound in recent technical ranges amid little reason to break far in either direction, market sources said.
June slipped one cent to close at $2.196 per million British thermal units. July settled 2.3 cents lower at $2.224. Other months ended mixed, with some 1999s up slightly.

"They tried to break it (futures) down early, but the Hub (cash) wouldn't break. Then we saw a little late afternoon selling, but we're still waiting for a breakout, and cash will have to take the lead," said one Midwest trader.

Despite recent stability, some expected a pullback ahead of the long, Memorial Day Holiday weekend, citing mostly mild U.S. weather forecasts and longs needing to exit before the June expiry on Wednesday.
Forecasts next week are calling for normal to slightly below-normal weather for the upper two-thirds of the nation, with some above-normal temperatures expected in Texas and parts of the Southeast.

Technical traders agreed there was little reason for a breakout. June support and resistance were still seen at $2.15 and $2.30, respectively. Major buying was likely at the $2.05 double bottom, with good selling expected at the contract high of $2.43.

In the cash, Gulf Coast swing prices were steady to up slightly Thursday to the high-teens. Midcon pipes were little changed in the low-$2s. New York city gate gas also held relatively steady in the mid-$2.40s.
Transco said 400 mmcfd of gas capacity on its Texas mainline, still cut this week due to planned maintenance, should be fully restored by tomorrow. The line has a capacity of 600 mmcfd.

Planned work on Mobil's Mary Ann gas processing plant in Coden, Ala., has cut the plant's total processing capacity of 380-390 mmcfd. About 120 mmcfd should be back by early next week, with the balance due back in three weeks.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip fell 0.8 cent to $2.264. NYMEX said 52,039 contracts traded, up from Wednesday's revised tally of 38,150.

On the KCBT, June finished 2.5 cents lower at $2.045, while deferreds ended steady to down 2.5 cents. The East/West spread widened by 1.5 cents to 15.1 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 334 lots traded, up from Wednesday's total of 291.
